prompt:
The packing hall has to clear this pallet through the customer's goods-in scanner tonight, so the last case off the line is photographed on the labelling bench before it goes to the wrapper.

A case stands on the bench with its logistics label applied to the side panel: a barcode with a single line of bracketed human-readable text under it. The same panel already carries the production date stamp, inked 26 09 04 for year, month and day, and a net weight plate reading 12.5 kg. The identifier table lies open on the bench beside the case: identifier 11 takes a production date written as year, then month, then day, each as a pair of figures; identifier 3103 takes a net weight in kilograms carried to three decimal places.

What the label line itself carries is what the bench table does not say.
easy_question: Does this photograph show a cardboard case on a bench carrying a logistics label, an inked date stamp and a net weight plate on one panel? Answer yes or no only.

steps.ask: Compare the dated segment in the label line with the date stamp inked on the same panel and say how they stand. Answer with one of: the dated segment repeats the figures of the date stamp on the panel; the dated segment carries figures the panel's date stamp does not carry; the label line has no dated segment in it.
Count the figures printed inside the bracketed dated segment of the label line. Write the number only.
